sections.title: Air vibration and acoustic phonetics

teaching.text: **The shape of the tract becomes audible through the air inside it**. Acoustic phonetics studies that resulting sound and connects its pattern with the articulation that produced it.
children: Changes in tract shape alter how that air can vibrate. The resulting acoustic pattern carries information about the speech movements that shaped the passage.

teaching.text: Articulation concerns the configuration and movement of the organs, while acoustics concerns the resulting sound. Connecting the two explains how a physical movement becomes information available to a listener.

sections.title: Why scientific understanding of AI matters

teaching.text: **An impressive response is a behavior to explain rather than a complete explanation of its own mechanism**. Examining the computation helps connect the observed response with evidence about how it was produced.

teaching.text: Scientific reasoning asks what evidence supports a proposed explanation and what would distinguish it from another. Familiarity with a product or a confident-sounding answer does not settle those questions.

sections.title: Dynamical systems 1
Lecture agenda
A staged shortest-path problem

teaching.text: **A stored value includes the best continuation from a state to the goal**. Adding it to an immediate edge cost makes the comparison about the whole remaining route rather than its first step.
children: For each available next state, add the edge cost to that next state’s solved value. Choose the smallest resulting total to obtain the value for the current state.

teaching.text: Following the best total after the values are known is different from choosing the smallest edge before considering the future. The stored value carries the information the greedy choice leaves out.

sections.title: Why the locally cheapest choice can lose

teaching.text: **The next cheap move can be part of an expensive full route**. A greedy choice is fast because it considers immediate cost while leaving the remaining path out of that comparison.
children: The cost of a complete path is the sum of its successive edges. A locally favorable choice therefore does not establish that the total route is cheapest.

teaching.text: Greedy search is fast because it makes limited comparisons. That speed comes with the risk of missing the globally best solution in the illustrated shortest-path problem.

teaching.text: **Trying every route can establish the best answer in the finite path problem**. Its cost comes from evaluating many candidates, including repeated pieces shared by different routes.

teaching.text: Its strength is completeness, while its weakness is the cost of repeated calculation. Dynamic programming keeps the useful comparison while reusing shared partial solutions.

sections.title: Masses and Springs · Theory and Prediction
One mass, two directions

teaching.text: **The direction of movement can change while the reason for oscillation stays the same**. Motion along a spring and motion across a tensioned support both combine a restoring force with inertia.
children: In both arrangements, displacement produces a restoring force and inertia carries the mass past equilibrium. The direction of the drawing changes, but the competition between restoring force and continued motion remains.

teaching.text: The paired systems make it possible to recognize one physical mechanism in two geometries. The transverse example uses tension in its supports to provide the restoring effect.

sections.title: Mass and stiffness change the rate

teaching.text: **Frequency depends on how quickly a system can be pulled back and turned around**. A heavier moving part resists that reversal, while greater stiffness strengthens the pull that produces it.
children: More mass is harder to accelerate and reverse, so each cycle takes longer. A stiffer system supplies a stronger restoring force for the same displacement, so it completes the return more quickly.

teaching.text: A directional prediction requires saying which property changed and which property stayed fixed. When mass and stiffness both change, their effects must be considered together rather than applying either rule alone.

sections.title: Two masses have two normal modes

teaching.text: **Two connected masses have more than one way to move as a system**. They can travel together or oppose one another, and the opposing pattern puts more of the connecting structure to work.
children: Moving together leaves the middle connection relatively unstretched. Moving oppositely stretches that connection as well as the outer supports, adding restoring action and raising the frequency.

teaching.text: A normal mode is a whole pattern, not a separate frequency assigned to just one mass. Both masses participate in a mode, and combining the modes can produce more complicated motion.

sections.title: Pop quiz
Three masses have three normal modes

teaching.text: **The three modes are three arrangements of coordinated motion**. Their differences include whether the middle mass travels with the outer masses, stays still, or moves against its neighbors.

sections.title: One more mass, one more mode

teaching.text: **Adding a moving part adds another independent possibility for vibration**. A continuous string extends this idea to material distributed along its length rather than a few separately drawn blocks.

sections.title: A fixed–fixed string combines harmonics

sections.title: Reflection prompt

teaching.text: **Speaking continuously means the tract is continually changing its configuration**. The formant bands therefore trace transitions through a phrase rather than a sequence of perfectly isolated steady vowels.

sections.title: Forward flow and an illustrative output distribution

teaching.text: **A forward pass uses what the network currently knows to produce a decision**. Each processing stage transforms the values it receives and supplies the next stage with new activations.

sections.title: Predict how changing a marked weight affects error

teaching.text: **A useful correction depends on how a connection contributes and what the output should become**. Raising a weight can help or hurt depending on the incoming sign and the category’s current error.

teaching.text: **A sequence needs a way for information from one step to matter at the next**. Recurrent state provides such a connection, allowing current processing to depend on prior context.

sections.title: One prediction task for different sequences

teaching.text: **Prediction can be organized around the same question across different kinds of data**. Once the sequence is represented as vectors, the model uses the available context to assign support to possible continuations.
children: The model uses the available context to assign probabilities to possible continuations. Learning improves those probabilities when the actual continuation supplies feedback.

teaching.text: A token’s position in the sequence and its context help determine what should come next. The prediction task stays recognizable even when the represented material changes from words to another kind of signal.

sections.title: Which sequences can be English words?

teaching.text: **A language restricts which sound sequences fit particular syllable positions**. A combination allowed across a syllable break can still be excluded from the beginning of a single syllable.
children: An onset occurs before a syllable’s vowel, and a coda occurs after it. A cluster that works across a syllable boundary does not necessarily work at the beginning of a syllable.

teaching.text: The spelling examples provide clues to these restrictions, but letters and speech sounds are different units. The beginning of knee, for example, contains written k even though its ordinary pronunciation does not begin with /k/.

sections.title: Guessing the next letter reveals phonotactic knowledge

teaching.text: **A short word beginning already carries information about what can follow**. Learning its likely completions requires capturing those restrictions rather than choosing every next letter equally.
children: Some beginnings permit many continuations while others sharply restrict the possibilities. A probability distribution can express that difference by spreading probability broadly or concentrating it on fewer choices.

teaching.text: Learning from many such completions can capture regularities without receiving a separate verbal rule for each one. The spelling exercise probes useful language knowledge while remaining distinct from a complete description of English phonology.

sections.title: Design an agentic system for English syllables

teaching.text: **A computational task can be organized through explicit instructions, learned parameters or communication among models**. The three software categories separate those roles while allowing them to be combined in one working system.
children: An explicitly written program specifies operations in a language such as Python. A trained network instead stores useful input-to-output relationships in its weights, while an agentic arrangement can ask models to draft, check and revise the result.

teaching.text: These forms can work together in one system rather than replacing every earlier operation. Natural-language instructions can organize agents that still rely on trained parameters and executable software.
